# The starting skeleton

What `pds init` writes for each profile. Every record is a stub with `origin: skeleton`: a prompt to confirm, correct or delete, capped at `outlined` until a person does.

## SaaS product (`saas`)

115 seeds: 4 OBJ, 3 MET, 5 ACT, 5 ROLE, 6 PERM, 1 TEN, 5 SRF, 12 DOM, 52 CAP, 3 PLAN, 2 EXT, 5 TERM, 6 OBL, 6 QST.

### Domains and capabilities

| Domain | Module | Capabilities | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DOM-marketing-and-acquisition` Marketing and acquisition | core | Marketing site and content; Pricing and plan comparison; Lead capture and demo requests; Attribution and referrals | How people find, evaluate and start using the product. |
| `DOM-identity-and-access` Identity and access | identity | Sign-up and account creation; Sign-in, sessions and sign-out; Password and credential recovery; Multi-factor authentication; Single sign-on; Roles and permissions; Personal profile and preferences | Who people are and what they may do. |
| `DOM-workspaces-and-teams` Workspaces and teams | tenancy | Creating, switching and closing workspaces; Inviting and managing members; Workspace settings and branding; Tenant isolation and data boundaries | How customers and their people are grouped and kept apart. |
| `DOM-onboarding-and-activation` Onboarding and activation | core | First-run setup and guided start; Sample data and templates; Checklists and activation prompts | Getting a new customer to first value. |
| `DOM-core-product` Core product | core | The core job the product does | Replace this with the product's own domains: what it does for its customers. Everything else in this map is the scaffolding around it. |
| `DOM-billing-and-plans` Billing and plans | commercial | Plans, pricing and entitlements; Subscription: trial, start, change, cancel, renew; Payment methods and checkout; Invoices and receipts; Failed payments and dunning; Tax, VAT and currency; Usage metering and limits; Refunds, credits and disputes | How access is packaged, priced, charged and collected. |
| `DOM-notifications-and-messaging` Notifications and messaging | lifecycle-comms | Transactional email; In-app notifications; Notification preferences and consent; Lifecycle and product-update messages | Everything the product says to people unprompted. |
| `DOM-integrations-and-api` Integrations and API | integrations | Public API; API keys and OAuth apps; Outbound webhooks; Connections to other products; Data import and export | How the product connects to other products and to developers. |
| `DOM-insights-and-reporting` Insights and reporting | core | Dashboards and reports; Scheduled and shared reports | What customers see about their own usage and results. |
| `DOM-administration-and-support` Administration and support | back-office | Customer and plan administration; Customer support tools; Support access to a customer account; Audit log; Feature flags and rollouts | What the company's own staff use to run the product and help customers. |
| `DOM-trust-and-compliance` Trust, privacy and compliance | compliance | Data export and deletion requests; Consent, terms and privacy notices; Data retention and deletion schedules; Security controls and incident response | What the product owes its customers and the law. |
| `DOM-platform-and-operations` Platform and operations | core | Monitoring, logging and alerting; Backup and disaster recovery; Environments, releases and rollback; Performance and capacity; Product analytics instrumentation | What keeps the product running, observable and recoverable. |

### Foundational questions

| Question | Module | Blocking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who is the customer, who pays and who uses the product? | core | yes |
| What is the one job the product does that customers will pay for? | core | yes |
| How are customers and their people grouped: account, company or workspace? | tenancy | yes |
| How does the product charge: free tier, seats, usage, tiers or a mix? | commercial | yes |
| Where may customer data be stored and processed? | compliance | yes |
| Is the product self-serve, sales-led or both? | core | no |
